newsitem.title: UK: Protestant shot dead in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Protestant shot dead in Northern Ireland.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead a leading pro-British Loyalist in Belfast on Wednesday in a suspected Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrilla ambush.
Police would not confirm the identity of the dead man, who was shot in an office in the heart of Shankill, a Protestant stronghold in west Belfast.
Loyalist sources and residents said that the victim was a former guerrilla, Robert "Basher" Bates, who had served prison terms for crimes during Northern Ireland's long-running conflict.
Police declined to say if the shooting was linked to the conflict which has pitted rival guerrillas against each other in a bitter battle over British sovereignty of Northern Ireland.
A leading Loyalist politician, John White, of the Ulster Democratic Party, blamed the IRA which has stepped up hostilities in the province since abandoning a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.
"Apparently two men walked into the office on foot and shot him twice in the head and made their escape," he told Reuters.
"I think it has profound consequences for the Loyalist ceasefire. Obviously this man was well respected in this community....It is a new twist in the IRA's campaign."

The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule, has killed two soldiers in bomb and gun attacks since October last year. A breakaway left-wing group, the Irish National Liberation Army, shot dead an off-duty policeman in a Belfast pub last month.

Loyalist guerrillas, who want to maintain the province's links with Britain, have killed two Catholic nationalists in attacks in recent months, although Loyalist commanders say a truce they called in October 1994 is still in force.
